items.title: Gulf oil exports plunge 49% as Hormuz bypass routes fall short

featured_image.name: Two pipelines helping Saudi Arabia, UAE bypass the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
More than a month into the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the full scale of the disruption to global energy flows is becoming clear. Seaborne crude exports from Gulf states excluding Iran collapsed to 8.44 million barrels per day in March, a 49% drop from February's 16.58 million barrels, according to Arab economic reports cited by Calcalist. Despite weeks of logistical mobilization across the region, improvised bypass routes through Saudi pipelines, the UAE's Fujairah port, and Iraqi overland convoys have managed to replace only about half of normal export volumes.[1]

The disruption, triggered by Iran's effective blockade of the strait following the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran that began on February 28, has reshaped the global oil market. S&P Global Ratings raised its 2026 oil price assumptions by $15 per barrel in March, to $80 for Brent and $75 for WTI, citing expectations of prolonged disruption. Energy prices have surged well above those forecasts, with Brent crude recently trading near the $109 range and analysts at Macquarie Group warning prices could reach $150 if the strait remains closed through April.[2][3][4]

items.title: Iran launches drone strikes on US bases in UAE, Kuwait

featured_image.name: Iran attacks cause fire in Kuwait, Bahrain; kill man in UAE - Al Jazeera

items.description: Iran's military launched a fresh wave of drone strikes against American military positions in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait on Saturday, targeting radar systems and command infrastructure in what Tehran described as the second phase of its retaliatory operations against the US-Israeli alliance. The escalation came as the conflict, which began on February 28, entered its sixth week.

items.title: China, Russia call for ceasefire as Trump's Iran deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Sunday that achieving a ceasefire is the "fundamental way" to resolve the navigation crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a Xinhua dispatch from Beijing. Wang made the remarks during a phone conversation with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, as President Donald Trump's Monday deadline for Iran to reopen the strait draws near.[1]

items.title: Israel says Iran still holds 1,000-plus missiles five weeks into war
items.description:
More than five weeks into the war between Israel and Iran, Tehran's use of cluster munition-equipped ballistic missiles has emerged as one of the conflict's defining and most troubling tactics, scattering small explosive bomblets across Israeli population centers in attacks that bypass the country's layered air defense systems.

An Israeli Air Force intelligence officer publicly disclosed for the first time on April 4 that the military believes Iran still retains more than 1,000 ballistic missiles capable of reaching Israel. "The Iranians have more than 1,000 missiles that are capable of reaching Israel," Lt. Col. "Tet," who leads research on Iran's missiles and drones in the IAF's Air Intelligence Group, told Israel's Channel 12 news. At the war's outset, the IDF assessed Iran held approximately 2,500 ballistic missiles. Iran has since fired over 500 at Israel, launched hundreds more at Gulf states, and potentially lost hundreds in strikes on its launchers and depots.[1]

items.title: Iraqi oil tanker transits Hormuz after Iran exemption

featured_image.name: Iraqi crude tanker passes through Strait of Hormuz after Iran transit  exemption - The Economic Times

items.description: Iran announced on Saturday that Iraq would be exempt from all restrictions on maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could partially reopen the flow of Iraqi crude oil after more than five weeks of near-total shutdown at the world's most critical energy chokepoint.

items.title: Iranian missiles hit Negev chemical complex for third time

featured_image.name: Iran strike hits industrial zone in southern Israel

items.description: Iran launched multiple waves of ballistic missiles at Israel on Saturday and into Sunday, striking the Neot Hovav industrial zone south of Beersheba and scattering cluster munitions across central Israel in an escalation of the six-week-old conflict. The attacks wounded at least six people and caused widespread damage to residential buildings and infrastructure across several cities.
